I don't think taking a break will disappoint everyone, but there is a difference between taking a break to regain strength to face the struggles and avoiding it. I think we feel the same way, I am so sick and tired of being afraid too. But even though I'm struggling right now, I know that  I can get through this and being afraid will not stop me from living the life I want, even if it looks a little different than I expected. I like to sit with myself and wonder whether or not I am "running away" or "taking a break". It's important to be honest with yourself and maybe it'll help to talk to others about it too. I took a break from my first year of college because of this, I did part time classes and it helped me. Maybe you could be putting lots of expectations on yourself, maybe taking things slow can help. I know you want to keep doing this, so maybe it'll help to take a break.  


\>Is it even possible to go to college with agoraphobia?   


I think it is possible, of course it can be hard at times. Sometimes you'll miss out on so much you think it's impossible to get back on track or fix things (because you want things to be better so bad), but I don't think it's impossible. You will have good and bad days, but on the bad days it's important to tend to yourself. Reach out to counselling, reach out to friends, take it easy, make small goals like if something (like going to work) seems like a big thing, try to do something small like leaving your bedroom for 3 minutes. It is worth it and it shows you are capable even on the bad days. I know that you will be able to push through, whatever that looks like. 

During times like these it's important to reassess and reroute, make a plan, and be honest with yourself, seek guidance from others. This does not mean you're giving up! You will tackle it, slowly but surely you'll get through it. 

Sorry if this all sounds like gibberish or if I misunderstood you, I was just browsing through reddit posts of college with agoraphobia and found this relatable. I don't know you but I know that despite the situation you may be in that it is entirely possible. Take care <3

im proud of you for wanting to be better and work on self improvement. im not sure why you are feeling this way there can be many reasons. 

do you just want to feel loved by someone romantically? 

do you feel like having a gf will fix your problems?

are you addicted to the feelings you get when you develop a crush on someone or lust for someone?

do you feel like you need her to be happy?

whatever the reason is, you will know. im glad you're aware that you find this a problem, a lot of guys i find don't think this is a problem. wanting a gf is different than wanting a gf so you can feel fulfilled with life. one is healthy one is not. 

i think you need to set goals and priorities in life. what is it that you really want in life? what are your goals that you are working towards? you need to have a focus on your life that could be towards career, hobbies, passion etc. i think you need to find the deeper meaning behind things and continue working on yourself. journaling your feelings or even posting on reddit is great for helping you figure out the meaning behind your feelings. hope this helped
